summary.text: A probability distribution describes how probabilities are assigned to the possible results of a random phenomenon.
It is closely linked to random variables: a random variable assigns a value to each outcome and so induces a distribution on the values it can take.
Discrete distributions are described by probability mass functions, while many continuous distributions use probability density functions.

facts.label: Fair coin
facts.value: Heads (1) and tails (0) each get probability 1/2

facts.label: Discrete tool
facts.value: Described with a probability mass function

facts.label: Continuous tool
facts.value: Many are described with a probability density function

facts.label: Continuous outcomes
facts.value: Only events with infinitely many outcomes, like intervals, can exceed zero

facts.label: Univariate versus multivariate
facts.value: One random variable, or two or more together

items.prompt: A supermarket scale can show as many digits as you like. What is the chance that a piece of ham weighs exactly 500 g?

options.label: A small but positive chance
About one half
Zero
It depends on the scale's brand

items.explain: No matter how many digits are shown, there could always be further non-zero digits, so an exact weight has probability zero.

items.prompt: A pack of ham labelled "500 g" must weigh between 490 g and 510 g. Why can that requirement have a real chance of being met when an exact weight cannot?

options.label: The scale rounds every weight to the nearest gram
An interval covers many outcomes, so it can have positive probability
Weights are always whole numbers of grams
Exact weights are likelier than intervals

items.explain: For a continuous variable only events with infinitely many outcomes, such as intervals, can have probability above zero. The requirement allows some tolerance.

items.prompt: Which of these would be described with a probability mass function rather than a density function?

options.label: The temperature at noon tomorrow
The weight of a pack of ham
The height of the next person to walk in
The number showing on a rolled die

items.explain: A die roll has a discrete set of outcomes, so it uses a mass function. Temperature and weight vary over a continuous range.

items.prompt: A study records each person's height and weight together as a pair. What kind of distribution describes the pair?

options.label: A multivariate distribution
A univariate distribution
A discrete list of one number
A distribution with no sample space

items.explain: A multivariate distribution gives probabilities for a list of two or more random variables; a univariate one covers a single variable.

items.prompt: A delivery company wants the chance a parcel arrives in no more than a chosen number of hours, for any limit it picks. Which function gives that?

options.label: The probability mass function
The sample space
The cumulative distribution function
The univariate distribution

items.explain: The cumulative distribution function gives the probability that the variable is no larger than a given value.

items.prompt: A coin toss is recorded as 1 for heads and 0 for tails. What has been set up?

options.label: A sample space with no outcomes
A way of making the coin biased
A continuous distribution
A function that gives each outcome a value

items.explain: That is a random variable: a function that assigns a value to each outcome, which in turn gives a distribution on those values.
